table.name: customers
table.purpose: Master list of customers (likely a Czech fuel-card / fuel-retail business, given the gasstations, products and transactions tables). One row per customer with its identifier, account segment and billing currency. Referenced by the yearmonth and transactions_1k tables.

Currency.name: Currency
Currency.description: Customer's billing/contract currency: Czech koruna (CZK) for the vast majority, euro (EUR) for a small minority.

CustomerID.name: CustomerID
CustomerID.description: Unique customer identifier; primary key of the customers table, referenced by yearmonth and transactions_1k.

Segment.name: Segment
Segment.description: Customer segment code with three levels, likely a sales/account-tier classification: SME (small and medium enterprises, the bulk), LAM and KAM (plausibly Large Account Management and Key Account Management, i.e. larger customers). The exact expansion of LAM/KAM is not verifiable from the data alone.

table.name: gasstations
table.purpose: Reference/dimension table of gas stations (one row per station, 5716 stations in the Czech Republic and Slovakia). Each station belongs to a chain (ChainID), is located in a country, and is classified by market segment. It is referenced by transactions_1k, which records sales at these stations. The database appears to be a fuel-retail sales dataset (customers, products, transactions, and a yearmonth time dimension).

ChainID.name: ChainID
ChainID.description: Identifier of the retail chain/brand that operates the gas station. Repeats across stations (233 distinct values, most common chains 3, 2, 33, 1, 4), so it groups stations under an operator. The detected joins to transactions_1k.TransactionID and products.ProductID are statistically accepted but semantically implausible (a chain ID should not reference a transaction or product ID); likely spurious.

Country.name: Country
Country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 country code of the gas station's location: CZE (Czech Republic, 4836 stations) and SVK (Slovakia, 880 stations).

GasStationID.name: GasStationID
GasStationID.description: Unique identifier of the gas station; primary key of the table (5716 distinct values, one per row). Referenced by transactions_1k.GasStationID, linking transactions to the station where they occurred.

Segment.name: Segment
Segment.description: Market positioning/segment of the gas station brand: 'Premium', 'Value for money', 'Discount', 'Noname' (unbranded/independent), or 'Other'. A 5-level categorical attribute of the station.

table.name: products
table.purpose: Lookup/catalog table of products and services sold at gas stations (fuel, AdBlue, tolls, fees, groceries, spare parts, card services), one row per product, referenced by the transactions table. Descriptions are mostly in Czech, suggesting a Czech fuel-station/fleet-card context.

Description.name: Description
Description.description: Human-readable name/label of the product or service sold at gas stations (Czech, e.g. 'Katalyzátor' = catalytic converter, 'Potraviny' = food/groceries, 'Servisní poplatek' = service fee, 'Vydání karty' = card issuance). Includes fuel-related items (AdBlue), toll-related items (Toll access-Austria, Toll DEU Correction Prepayment), and various fees and services. Not unique — some descriptions repeat for different ProductIDs.

ProductID.name: ProductID
ProductID.description: Primary key of the products table: unique numeric identifier of a product or service. Referenced by transactions_1k.ProductID (each transaction line is for one product). The statistical joins to transactions_1k.Amount and gasstations.ChainID are spurious (numeric overlap only) and should be ignored.

table.name: transactions_1k
table.purpose: A 1000-row sample of point-of-sale purchase transactions at gas stations: each row is one purchase by a customer (via a loyalty/payment card) of a product at a specific station on a given date and time, with the quantity (Amount, liters for fuel) and total price. Foreign keys link to customers, gasstations, and products; the yearmonth table presumably aggregates by month.

Amount.name: Amount
Amount.description: Quantity of product purchased. For fuel products this is the volume in liters (integer liters, range 0–264, median 19). The 0 values likely indicate non-fuel purchases or a missing/zero quantity. Joins to products.ProductID only in the sense that the unit depends on the product.

CardID.name: CardID
CardID.description: Identifier of the loyalty/payment card used for the transaction. Nearly unique per row (902 distinct in 1000 rows), values in the ~26k–776k range, unrelated to CustomerID values, so it is a separate card identifier rather than a customer key.

CustomerID.name: CustomerID
CustomerID.description: Identifier of the customer who made the purchase; references customers.CustomerID (many-to-one). 517 distinct customers in this 1000-row sample.

Date.name: Date
Date.description: Date of the transaction, stored as text in YYYY-MM-DD format. This 1000-row sample covers only 2012-08-23 through 2012-08-26.

GasStationID.name: GasStationID
GasStationID.description: Identifier of the gas station where the transaction occurred; references gasstations.GasStationID (many-to-one). 437 distinct stations appear in the sample.

Price.name: Price
Price.description: Total price of the transaction (not unit price): it is roughly proportional to Amount (e.g. 4 units → 3.64, 63 → 1445.97, 24 → 524.60), with implied per-unit prices varying by product/station. Currency unit is not evident from the data (unresolved).

ProductID.name: ProductID
ProductID.description: Identifier of the product purchased; references products.ProductID (many-to-one). 28 distinct products; the dominant IDs 2 (523 rows) and 5 (239 rows) are most likely fuel grades, with the remaining IDs being other station products.

Time.name: Time
Time.description: Time of day of the transaction, stored as text in HH:MM:SS format. Should be combined with Date for a full timestamp.

TransactionID.name: TransactionID
TransactionID.description: Primary key of the table; sequential integer 1–1000 identifying one purchase transaction. The reported 'referenced_by' join to gasstations.ChainID is spurious (a numeric-range coincidence), since a transaction ID cannot reference a chain.

table.name: yearmonth
table.purpose: Monthly aggregation of customer consumption: one row per customer per month (CustomerID + YYYYMM month), summarizing that customer's total consumption for the month. It is a pre-aggregated companion to the transactions_1k detail table, covering Dec 2011 – Nov 2013 for ~30,566 customers. The unit of Consumption (currency vs. volume) is not determinable from the data alone.

Consumption.name: Consumption
Consumption.description: Total consumption of the customer in the given month. Units are not directly evidenced; given the related gasstations/products/transactions tables, this is plausibly a monetary amount spent (or volume of fuel purchased) aggregated per customer-month. Negative values (min -582092.86) indicate refunds, corrections or reversed transactions. The very large max (2,052,187.11) suggests a few heavy outliers or data errors.

CustomerID.name: CustomerID
CustomerID.description: Identifier of the customer whose monthly consumption is recorded; references customers.CustomerID (many-to-one).

Date.name: Date
Date.description: Month identifier stored as a string in YYYYMM format (e.g. 201205 = May 2012). Range 201112–201311, i.e. December 2011 through November 2013. Not a real date type.
